signals.title: Intel, SK hynix shares surge following reports of chip packaging partnership - SK is said to be testing Intel's 2.5D EMIB for HBM integration - Tom's Hardware
signals.summary: Tom's Hardware reports that Intel and SK hynix shares rose after reports that SK hynix is testing Intel's 2.5D EMIB packaging for HBM integration. For conductor etch, the signal matters because HBM integration and advanced packaging can shift customer priorities toward packaging-linked process capacity and etch-intensive foundry demand.

signals.title: Intel 14A Node Enters Risk Production in 2028, 10A and 7A Nodes on the Roadmap - TechPowerUp
signals.summary: TechPowerUp reports that Intel's 14A node is expected to enter risk production in 2028, with 10A and 7A also appearing on the roadmap. The update is relevant to conductor etch because node-roadmap credibility and EUV cadence influence when advanced process complexity converts into tool demand.

signals.title: Intel's foundry reset: 14A, 10A and tougher engineering rules - digitimes
signals.summary: digitimes reports that Intel is resetting its foundry roadmap around 14A, 10A, and stricter engineering rules. For conductor etch, this is a roadmap execution signal: tighter process discipline and node timing can affect when leading-edge capacity and etch process steps move toward volume.

signals.title: AMD Ramps EPYC Venice Production on TSMC 2nm - Let's Data Science
signals.summary: Let's Data Science reports that AMD is ramping EPYC Venice production on TSMC's 2nm process. This matters to conductor etch because a high-volume server CPU ramp on a leading-edge node is a direct indicator of process complexity, yield learning, and future tool intensity.

signals.title: Samsung Foundry Has Apparently Won A 2nm CPU Order From A North American Fabless Customer - Wccftech
signals.summary: Wccftech reports that Samsung Foundry may have won a 2nm CPU order from a North American fabless customer, with AMD identified in the report as the likely source. For conductor etch, this is a foundry-share and leading-node demand signal that could affect advanced-node capacity planning and etch tool timing.
